clinician.final_diagnosis: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma with lymph node metastases and paraneoplastic hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old male heavy smoker presented with a 6-month history of right shoulder and interscapular pain radiating to the anteromedial arm and clavicular area. Physical examination revealed striking findings consistent with paraneoplastic hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (HOA): clubbing of fingers and toes, pachydermia with skin thickening of the scalp, forehead, and fingers, enlarged large joints with tubular swollen extremities, and right lateral cervical lymphadenopathy (1 cm). Pain was exacerbated by pressure on the distal radius and ulna but not related to cervical spine movement. CT imaging of the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis revealed a 23×19 mm mass in the right upper lobe dorsal segment with speculated margins, contrast enhancement, areas of necrosis, and pleural invasion, along with multiple mediastinal lymphadenopathy with central necrosis. Skeletal imaging confirmed symmetric periostosis with linear halving of the diaphysis and increased bone circumference, diagnostic of HOA. Laboratory findings showed inflammatory syndrome, slight anemia, and markedly elevated VEGF (1291 pg/mL, normal <100 pg/mL). The patient received NSAIDs and opioids for pain management, was referred to Oncology, and underwent treatment with chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and gamma-knife radiotherapy. Despite these interventions, the disease progressed and the patient died 9 months later.
